did_you_know.text: Did you know? The cubit was an ancient unit of length, so the Ark’s length is estimated at about 1.1–1.3 meters rather than one exact modern measurement.
Did you know? The Sages saw the gold inside and outside as a model for a person whose inner values match outward behavior.
Did you know? The word “mikshah” describes an object shaped from one piece of gold rather than assembled from separate parts.
Did you know? The Sages interpreted the cherubs facing one another as a symbol of the relationship between the people and God when Israel follows God’s will.
Did you know? A “tefach” was an ancient length measure based roughly on the width of a hand, so its exact size varied across places and periods.
Did you know? Describing the menorah as one hammered piece means that its decorations, branches, and base were regarded as one continuous and highly complex work.
Did you know? The word “meshukadim” is connected with the almond tree because the menorah’s cups were shaped like almond blossoms; almond trees are also known for flowering early.
Did you know? A “talent” was an ancient unit of weight, not a coin. Its exact weight varied, so it cannot be converted into one certain number of kilograms.
Did you know? The “horns” at the corners of the incense altar were not animal horns, but raised projections built into the altar’s design.
Did you know? The word “roḳe’aḥ” is connected with preparing fragrant mixtures; in the ancient world, this required carefully combining oils, perfumes, and spices.
